sources.title: Toyotomi clan
sources.note: Infobox founded 1585 (the name Toyotomi from the emperor), dissolved 1615; unification of Japan 1590; Hideyoshi died 1598, Hideyori deposed 1600 after Sekigahara; Hideyori and Yodo-dono seppuku at Osaka Castle; five regents.

sources.title: Toyotomi Hideyori
sources.note: Born 28 Aug 1593; head of the clan 1598-1615; Ieyasu seized control in 1600 after Sekigahara; winter siege 1614, summer siege 5 June 1615; died 4 June 1615 at Osaka Castle.

sources.title: Siege of Osaka
sources.note: Winter campaign 8 Nov 1614 to 22 Jan 1615; moat filled; summer campaign May-June 1615; Tokugawa victory, Toyotomi clan destroyed; the shogunate obtained 650,000 koku at Osaka, a han under Matsudaira Tadayoshi, 1619 Osaka Jodai.

sources.title: Battle of Shizugatake
sources.note: Nagahama, Omi, Hideyoshi against Shibata Katsuie (20th day of the 4th month of Tensho 11); Kitanosho Castle in Echizen taken; Katsuie seppuku; Nobutaka forced to suicide June 1583; Nobukatsu a rival until Komaki and Nagakute 1584.

sources.title: Kyūshū campaign
sources.note: 1586 Shimazu seized Funai from the Otomo; 1587 Hidenaga landed in Bungo, Takajo in Hyuga, forced back to Satsuma; the Shimazu surrendered later in 1587, Kagoshima not attacked.

sources.title: Shimazu Yoshihisa
sources.note: Mid-1585 the Shimazu controlled Chikugo, Chikuzen, Hizen, Higo, Hyuga, Osumi and Satsuma, Otomo the main exception; 1587 settlement: most conquered domains went to Kato, Konishi and Kuroda, the Mori received fiefs in northern Kyushu, Kobayakawa gained Chikuzen, the Shimazu kept Satsuma, Osumi and half of Hyuga; Yoshihisa sued for peace in June 1587.

sources.title: Mōri Terumoto
sources.note: 1582 Hideyoshi besieged Takamatsu in Bitchu, after Honno-ji the Mori made peace; 1583 Terumoto became a vassal of Toyotomi Hideyoshi; 1.2 million koku at the peak; 1600 reduced to Nagato and Suo.

sources.title: Invasion of Shikoku
sources.note: June 1585 113,000 men in three armies; Chosokabe surrendered 6 Aug 1585; kept Tosa; Awa to Hachisuka Iemasa and Akamatsu Norifusa, Sanuki to Sengoku Hidehisa and Sogo Masayasu, Iyo to Kobayakawa Takakage and Mori generals; in 1583 Chosokabe controlled Iyo, Sanuki, Awa and Tosa.

sources.title: Siege of Odawara (1590)
sources.note: May to 4 August 1590; 220,000 against 82,000; Ieyasu given the Hojo lands; Ujimasa later forced to suicide.

sources.title: Toyotomi Hideyoshi
sources.note: Kampaku 6 Aug 1585 to 10 Feb 1592; Shizugatake 1583 some 30 provinces; Komaki-Nagakute 1584; Shikoku 1585; Kyushu 1586 or 1587; Odawara 1590; Senboku uprising Sept 1590; Kunohe rebellion Mutsu 13 March to 4 Sept 1591; Korea 1592; died 18 Sept 1598 at Fushimi Castle.

sources.title: Azuchi–Momoyama period
sources.note: After 1584 complete control of Kyoto and ruler of the former Oda domains; Chosokabe surrendered July 1585; Kyushu 1586-1587; Nagasaki occupied 1587; Odawara 1590; Korea April 1592, Seoul by May, Pyongyang within three months, withdrawn to the south by Jan 1593, second invasion 1597; 1598 survey 18.5 million koku, 2 million directly Hideyoshi, 2.5 million Ieyasu in the Kanto.

sources.title: Sengoku period
sources.note: 1585 Shikoku pacified; 1587 Kyushu pacified; 1590 Odawara, Kanto pacified, Tohoku clans swore allegiance; 1591 Kunohe Masazane defeated by Hideyoshi and Ieyasu; 1592-98 invasions of Korea; 1600 Sekigahara, Eastern Army under Ieyasu defeats the Western Army of Toyotomi loyalists; 1615 the last Toyotomi opposition stamped out.

sources.title: Akechi Mitsuhide
sources.note: 21 June 1582 Honno-ji; 2 July 1582 the Battle of Yamazaki.

sources.title: Ishiyama Hongan-ji War
sources.note: In 1583 Hideyoshi began building Osaka Castle on the Ishiyama site.

notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from fourteen pages (Toyotomi clan, Toyotomi Hideyori, Siege of Osaka, Battle of Shizugatake, Kyūshū campaign, Shimazu Yoshihisa, Mōri Terumoto, Invasion of Shikoku, Siege of Odawara (1590), Toyotomi Hideyoshi, Azuchi–Momoyama period, Sengoku period, Akechi Mitsuhide, Ishiyama Hongan-ji War for the Osaka Castle year). A regime inside Cliopatria's single Warring States Japan row; the Cliopatria shape is all Japan, so this is a fine-grained internal unit. Drawn: Hideyoshi's own lands of 1582, Echizen (1583), the former Oda domains (1584, the Oda dossier's shape), Awa, Sanuki and Iyo (1585), Kyushu outside Satsuma, Ōsumi and half of Hyūga (1587, from the Shimazu Yoshihisa page: lands to Katō, Konishi, Kuroda, the Mōri and Kobayakawa; which half of Hyūga is the researcher's reading), the Osaka fief alone from 1600 (the Hōjō lands that went to Ieyasu in 1590 are the tokugawa-clan dossier's, tinted here as a vassal holding) (a 35 km circle; the pages give 650,000 koku). Tinted vassals (not drawn in the keyframes): the Mōri (1583, the Mōri dossier's 1571 lands), Tosa (Chōsokabe, 1585), Satsuma, Ōsumi and half of Hyūga (Shimazu, 1587), Tōhoku (1590) and the Tokugawa clan on the Hōjō lands (1590); Tosa, Satsuma, Tōhoku and the Tokugawa tint ended in 1600 by bridging; the Mōri tint ends in 1600 on the Terumoto page (cut to Nagato and Suō). Not on the pages and so absent: the Mōri lands beyond the Terumoto page (drawn only as a vassal tint from 1583), Hokuriku, Shinano, Kai and Echigo (Uesugi, Aizu in 1598), the Maeda, the Tokugawa lands before 1590 and the Date conquest of Aizu in 1589 (the Sengoku page mentions it); the 'some 30 provinces' of 1583 and the 18.5 million koku with 2 million direct (1598) are numbers only. Page conflicts: the Kyūshū campaign page has the Shimazu seize Funai and Bungo in 1586 while the Yoshihisa page lists Bungo as the Ōtomo exception in mid-1585 and does not say they took it in 1586; the Chōsokabe page has about 100,000 men against Chōsokabe in 1585 and the Shikoku page 113,000; the Kyushu campaign is 1586 on the Hideyoshi body and the campaign page's start and 1587 in the Hideyoshi introduction and the Sengoku page; Osaka Castle is 1582 (start), 1583 (Ishiyama page), 1586 (Azuchi–Momoyama page) and 1597 (completion); the Shizugatake page dates by the Japanese calendar. The Toyotomi clan page's infobox dates the clan 1585 to 1615; this state starts at Yamazaki (July 1582). Counterparts: 'oda-clan', 'later-hojo-clan', 'tokugawa-shogunate' exist; 'chosokabe-clan' and 'shimazu-clan' need dossiers (see the counterpart list); the others are persons or groups. Area comparison not applicable (no infobox area).
